title: The Mice and the Cat

full_text:
The mice of a grand manor house were living in constant terror of a sleek, silent cat whose soft velvet paws made no sound as she stalked the corridors. Night after night, another mouse vanished into her claws. Desperate to find a remedy, the mice convened a solemn council in the dark pantry to devise a strategy for their collective survival.

Many plans were proposed and rejected. Finally, a young, dapper mouse of bold eloquence stepped forward, twirled his whiskers, and addressed the assembly:

"Gentlemen, our peril arises entirely from the stealth of our enemy! She pounces upon us unawares. The solution is remarkably simple: we must purchase a small, brass bell and suspend it from a ribbon around the cat's neck! Whenever she approaches, the bell will jingle: ting-a-ling! We will hear her coming from afar and easily scamper into our holes!"

The council erupted into wild applause. Mice stamped their paws, embraced in joy, and voted the young orator a great genius.

In the midst of the celebration, an ancient, scarred mouse who had sat quietly in the corner rose to his feet. He cleared his throat and looked around the room:

"The proposal is undoubtedly brilliant, my young friend. But before we adjourn the meeting, permit me to ask one simple question: which one among you is going to put the bell upon the cat?"

A dead, freezing silence fell over the pantry. The mice looked at one another, slipped their heads down, and one by one crept quietly away into the wainscot, learning that grand ideas are worthless unless there is someone brave enough to execute them.
moral: It is easy to propose impossible remedies; practical courage is what matters.
